title: Tamsin and the Wolf
premise: Gideon Crane, a runaway apprentice hiding in the valley where magic cannot follow, discovers their own face in a century-old book of prophecies alongside a date that falls tonight. Drawn out of the valley by the prophecy's pull, Gideon falls in with Tamsin, a wolf-shifter and last heir of a deposed royal line, whose father still wears a crown that has become a living parasite. As the moon wanes toward its thirteenth turn, Gideon learns their hedge-witch training was never an accident: they were raised as the unbinding key. In the climax beneath the ruined palace, Gideon must choose between erasing their own memories to fuel the unbinding or letting Tamsin's father die wearing the crown; they split the cost instead, losing only their memory of the valley while freeing the king. The story ends with Gideon and Tamsin walking into exile together, found family forged in place of everything forgotten.
about_author: Cyrus Fairweather is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing estate libraries in northern England before turning to fiction full-time. They write fantasy about inheritance, small magics, and the people history forgets to record.

chapters.title: The Valley That Forgets
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Establishes daily life tending the hedge-witch Maren's garden inside the valley where magic dies at the tree line. Gideon tends bees, brews charms that never quite work, and hides from the past. Emotional beat: restless safety, the ache of being invisible on purpose.

chapters.title: A Date Written in Ink
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Sorting Maren's newly inherited books, Gideon finds a prophecy ledger from a century ago bearing tonight's date and a sketch of their own face. Maren goes pale and orders them to stay indoors. Emotional beat: dread blooming under curiosity.

chapters.title: Thirteen Moons to Midnight
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. She reveals the prophecy: a king bound to his crown, a wolf heir, and a nameless key born outside magic. She confesses she took Gideon in to keep them hidden. Emotional beat: betrayal softened by fierce protectiveness.

chapters.title: The Wolf at the Tree Line
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. A wounded wolf collapses at the valley's edge, unable to cross. Gideon drags it over the boundary and it becomes Tamsin, bleeding and furious, pursued by crown-sent hunters. Emotional beat: first contact, mutual suspicion.

chapters.title: What Magic Cannot Follow
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Recovering in the valley, Tamsin explains the truth: her father King Aldric wears a crown that eats its wearers, and the prophecy names her bloodline's end at the thirteenth moon. Emotional beat: grief worn as anger.

chapters.title: Leaving the Garden
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Hunters breach the valley using a stolen charm; Maren holds them off and shoves Gideon and Tamsin through the boundary. Crossing it, Gideon feels magic flood in for the first time. Emotional beat: terror and exhilaration entwined.

chapters.title: Roadside Charms
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. On the road toward the capital, Tamsin teaches Gideon basic craft while dodging patrols. Gideon's spells work too well, confirming they are no ordinary apprentice. Emotional beat: wary partnership becoming friendship.

chapters.title: The Inn of Small Prophets
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. At a waystation inn, a blind seer reads Gideon's palm and recoils: their future pages are already written. Tamsin buys silence with her mother's ring. Emotional beat: the weight of predestination.

chapters.title: Crown-Sentinels
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Ambushed by Sentinels wearing crown-forged iron, Tamsin shifts to protect Gideon and is captured. Gideon escapes with the prophecy ledger. Emotional beat: guilt sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: The Unbinding Key
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Alone, Gideon deciphers the ledger's marginalia: the key must unbind the king by paying memory as toll. They realize Maren erased their childhood deliberately. Emotional beat: identity shaken to the root.

chapters.title: Into the Pale Court
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Disguised as a charm-seller, Gideon infiltrates the capital during the Moonfast festival, guided by a pickpocket named Wren who owes Tamsin a life-debt. Emotional beat: fear transmuted into audacity.

chapters.title: The Thing Wearing His Crown
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. In the dungeons, Tamsin is brought before her father and sees the crown's parasite speaking through him, wearing his love like a mask. Emotional beat: horror and heartbreak in one breath.

chapters.title: Wren's Bargain
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren helps Gideon reach the cells but demands payment: after the unbinding, Gideon will remember nothing of the journey, so Wren promises to carry the story for them. Emotional beat: loyalty offered without expectation.

chapters.title: Cell Beneath the Chapel
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Reunion with Tamsin through a grate; they plan the unbinding for the thirteenth moon's eclipse. Tamsin refuses to let Gideon pay the full toll. Emotional beat: tenderness hardening into shared purpose.

chapters.title: Moonfast Riots
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. The festival turns when the crown's hunger leaks into the city, sending citizens into frenzy. In the chaos, Gideon and Tamsin flee toward the old palace ruins. Emotional beat: panic giving way to clarity.

chapters.title: The Ruined Palace
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. They descend into the throne room where Aldric, half-devoured, begs for death rather than freedom. The crown offers Gideon their lost memories back if they walk away. Emotional beat: temptation at its most personal.

chapters.title: What Maren Erased
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. The crown floods Gideon with returned fragments: they are the child of the last unbinding, born to be spent once. Understanding Maren's flight, Gideon chooses a third path—splitting the toll. Emotional beat: grief resolved into agency.

chapters.title: The Thirteenth Turn
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Under the eclipsed moon, Tamsin holds her father steady while Gideon begins the unbinding, feeding it the valley from their memory. The crown screams. Emotional beat: sacrifice embraced without bitterness.

chapters.title: Unbound
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. The parasite tears free and burns; Aldric lives, hollowed but human. Gideon wakes remembering Tamsin's face but not why it matters—and finds that enough. Emotional beat: loss and grace held together.

chapters.title: A Kingdom Without a Crown
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Aldric abdicates; the council offers Tamsin the empty throne and she refuses it, naming Wren chronicler instead. The crown is melted into a bell. Emotional beat: inheritance redefined as choice.

chapters.title: The Story Wren Kept
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren reads aloud the chronicle of Gideon's journey, restoring what was paid. Gideon weeps not for the valley but for Maren, and writes her a letter they may never send. Emotional beat: mourning made bearable by witness.

chapters.title: Two Roads Out of the City
chapters.summary: Gideon's POV. Gideon and Tamsin leave the capital together, taking the road toward new country, a shared pack, and a family chosen rather than prophesied. Final line echoes the ledger: some dates are beginnings. Emotional beat: open-hearted hope.
